back: The festival remembering the coming of the Holy Spirit on the disciples in Jerusalem (Acts 2), fifty days after Easter; the birthday of the Church.
A person who dies rather than give up their faith.

front: What happened to Saul on the road to Damascus?
back: A light struck him down and the risen Jesus spoke to him; he became the apostle Paul.

front: What did the Council of Jerusalem decide?
back: Gentile believers did not have to be circumcised.

front: What did the Edict of Milan do, and when?
back: In 313 CE it gave Christians freedom of worship and the return of property.

front: Why was the Council of Nicaea called?
back: To settle a dispute about the nature of Christ; it rejected the teaching of Arius (325 CE).

front: Name three early centres of African Christianity.
Which Ethiopian king adopted Christianity in the fourth century?
back: Ezana of Aksum, helped by Frumentius.

front: Why did Christians suffer persecution under Rome?
back: They refused to worship the emperor and the Roman gods, which made them seem disloyal.
